correctness.rationale: With strict common women-side priority, first-priority man must receive his best choice or block; deleting the pair proves unique serial-dictatorship stable matching. Given k women remaining, the independent uniform next male permutation makes their ranking positions a uniform k-subset, so his positive Borda utility is its maximum with mass C(u-1,k-1)/C(n,k). Conditional distribution is constant irrespective of earlier matches, proving independence; woman utilities multiply deterministically to n!. Exact product law and mean n!(n+1)^(n-1) follow by telescoping k/(k+1). For V=U/(n+1), compare s-th moments to independent Beta(k,1), with common mean and each variance O(k^-2); uniformly summable relative moment errors yield limit of n^s∏_{k=1}^n k/(k+s)=s!, and moment determinacy proves Exp(1). Independently checked exact first moments for n=1,2,3,4,10,50 and normalized second moment approaching 2. Source verifier additionally exhausts 1,4,216,331776 male preference profiles for n<=4, not a proof of all n.

value.rationale: Positive-Borda two-sided Nash welfare is a motivated fairness criterion for stable matching. The master-list condition is a canonical baseline where equilibrium matching is unique; the exact factorization and nondegenerate Exp(1) limit characterize unusually persistent welfare fluctuations that cannot be inferred from uniqueness or the mean alone. A natural all-market-size probability law and limiting distribution is independently interesting despite elementary sampling ingredients.

limitations: Only unique master-list stable matching and positive Borda all-agent product; not general stable matching NSW optimization.
Desai 2026 primary full article inaccessible; novelty best-of-knowledge, not guaranteed.
